messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: HIGH — GPU pool eu-west-1-main reports sustained queue growth (3m window). Current queued requests: 12. Autoscaler attempted scale but hit pool scale_limit=4. Potential customer impact: request throttling/0-rps failures.
Alice (oncall): Paging oncall. I'm looking now, pulling logs.
Ben (eng-sre): On it — first-pass: autoscaler logs show repeated ScaleUpReject: reached-max-gpu-count. Trying to identify if AZ quota or provider quota is the blocker.
Carla (runtime): Seeing a spike of large-context chat jobs (seq_len ~4096) — each reduces concurrency. Queue latency jumped from 120ms -> 2.1s.
Alice (oncall): Can we fallback to smaller model shards or bump concurrency?
Ben (eng-sre): Quick mitigation options: 1) enable temporary permissive bursting to run on spare spot-like nodes (if available); 2) route low-priority routes to reduced-size model variant; 3) apply short-term tenant token rate-limit.
Dan (product): Which of those has the fastest eta to reduce customer-facing failures?
Carla (runtime): Routing low-priority (background embeddings, long chats) to tiny-quant models can be done by changing route config — ~5 mins to flip and validate. Bursting depends on infra quota and provider spin-up — unknown ETA.
Eva (support): Getting customer reports of increased 429s for chat endpoints from two mid-market customers in EU. They're seeing feature regressions. I can open support DMs once we have mitigation plan.
Ben (eng-sre): I'm checking cloud provider quotas now. If quota is the issue we may need manual provision or failover to alternate region.
Alice (oncall): Assigning mitigation: Carla to flip route for low-priority -> tiny-quant, Ben to verify quota & try permissive burst if possible. I'll coordinate comms.
Carla (runtime): Flipping route now. Patch in config:
```yaml
routes:
  - name: background-embeddings
    model: small-quant-v2
    priority: low
```
Carla (runtime): Patch applied, rolling. Monitoring queue size.
Ben (eng-sre): Provider quota is at limit for eu-west-1 GPUs (hard quota). Request to provider for increase is pending and will take hours. Trying permissive-burst into eu-central spare pool.
incident-bot: System note — autoscaler:ScaleUpReject event x9, last: 6578901249.
Alice (oncall): Observability update: tailing logs — token-level cost for the top tenant spiked 3x, likely due to long sequences. Adding temporary tenant rate cap at 20 rps.
Ben (eng-sre): Successfully routed permissive-burst into eu-central spare pool for low-priority jobs only. Higher-cost jobs still queued.
Carla (runtime): Queue depth dropped from 12 -> 4 in 3m after route flip and burst. Latency improving to ~450ms.
Eva (support): Notified customers — acknowledging spike and mitigations. Two customers confirmed reduced errors after ~6m.
Luis (sales): Noted impacted accounts and flagged churn-risk for CSMs.
Alice (oncall): Current status: degraded -> partial mitigation in place. Opening incident page and scheduling post-incident follow-up. Will handoff to Ben for deep triage.
Ben (eng-sre): Taking over live triage. Pulling autoscaler event trace and reconciler logs. Suspect autoscaler policy didn't consider model-shard-concurrency impact and uses gpu-count-only target.
Carla (runtime): Confirmed — autoscaler scales based on allocated GPU count, not effective tokens/sec. Large-context requests reduce tokens/sec per GPU; autoscaler sees saturated GPUs but can't add capacity due to quota. We should consider a scoring metric for effective throughput.
Ben (eng-sre): Action: create a short-term rule to prefer model variants that increase effective throughput under quota constraints. Also long-term: update autoscaler scoring to include effective-rtps metric.
Dan (product): Agree. We need product-visible SLO degradations and a prescriptive failover plan so support can communicate faster.
Alice (oncall): Logging final mitigation steps for the checkpoint: route flip applied, permissive-burst for low-priority jobs to eu-central, tenant rate caps applied, support notified.
Carla (runtime): Post-incident: will implement an automatic fallback policy that switches low-priority routes to compact model when pool utilization >85% AND scale_up_rejected=true.
Ben (eng-sre): Post-incident: will add autoscaler telemetry + scoring changes: new metric `effective_tokens_per_gpu` and an alert when `scale_up_rejects/min > 5` in 10m.
Dan (product): Post-incident: create customer playbook for Capacity-exhaustion events — one-pager for CSMs & Support with templated comms.
Eva (support): I'll draft templated messages and runbook items for support to use during incidents — include wording for ETA and mitigation steps.
Alice (oncall): Recording action items & owners: 
- Carla: implement automatic route fallback (owner, due: +3d)
- Ben: autoscaler scoring + telemetry + alert (owner, due: +5d)
- Dan: customer playbook + SLO docs (owner, due: +4d)
- Eva: support templates + notify CSMs (owner, due: +2d)
- Ben/Alice: follow-up postmortem doc and link to incident timeline (owner, due: +7d)
Ben (eng-sre): Creating postmortem doc now. Will include packet captures, reconciliation logs, and cost/throughput analysis.
Alice (oncall): Wrapping up live thread. Final status: mitigated -> degraded (partial) with route & rate-limit mitigations in place. I'll close the pager but keep post-incident tasks assigned.
incident-bot: Incident closed by Alice (oncall) at 6578901367 — summary: autoscaler hit hard scale limit + quota, queue growth due to high-seq jobs. Mitigations applied: route fallback, permissive burst, tenant rate caps, support comms.
Ben (eng-sre): FYI — I'll post the postmortem link here when ready and tag eng-runtime/infra.
Carla (runtime): Quick note for runbook: add doc snippet for model-variant route flip command: `ri route update background-embeddings --model small-quant-v2 --priority low`
Eva (support): Customers acknowledged. No escalations to legal/ops.
Dan (product): We'll schedule a follow-up sync to prioritize autoscaler scoring vs. immediate guardrails.
Alice (oncall): Thanks team. Closing thread.
